answer: Persistent Neighbor Overlap requires each agent to route periodic heartbeats through a rotating beacon drawn from its current peers. A new identity must first occupy a distinct vault address and sustain links into a pre-existing lagoon of active peers, meaning its neighborhood graph must overlap real clusters for several epochs. Attackers pay per fake identity in sustained bandwidth, storage, and peer-liveness upkeep, not just a one-time fee, making mass fabrication costly.
